Weighted-arithmetic Water Quality Index from pH, DO, BOD, TDS, hardness, chloride, sulphate, nitrate, fluoride, turbidity. Standards: BIS 10500 acceptable limits (pH 8.5, TDS 500, hardness 200, chloride 250, sulphate 200, fluoride 1.0, nitrate 10 as N, turbidity 5 NTU) plus DO 5 mg/L and BOD 3 mg/L (CPCB). Ideal values pH 7, DO 14.6. Weights = 1/standard. Each sub-index capped at 500. Computed from observed values only; needs >=8 of 10 parameters.
Excellent <=50, Good 50-100, Poor 100-200, Very_poor 200-300, Unfit >300.
wqi_class with Very_poor and Unfit merged (Unfit has very few rows).

CPCB designated-best-use class from DO, pH, BOD, total coliform: A (DO>=6, pH 6.5-8.5, BOD<=2, TC<=50), B (DO>=5, pH 6.5-8.5, BOD<=3, TC<=500), C (DO>=4, pH 6-9, BOD<=3, TC<=5000), otherwise D_E (merged).

BIS 10500:2012 limits on dissolved chemistry only (pH 6.5-8.5, TDS, hardness, chloride, sulphate, fluoride, nitrate). Potable = all within acceptable limits; Treatment_needed = all within permissible limits but some above acceptable; Not_potable = any beyond permissible. Permissible: TDS 2000, hardness 600, chloride 1000, sulphate 400, fluoride 1.5. Turbidity and coliform are NOT used (raw surface water almost always exceeds them; they are removed by treatment).
Strict binary: 1 = Potable class (all dissolved-chemistry parameters within acceptable limits), else 0. Suggested drinkable / not-drinkable target.
Binary: 1 = Potable or Treatment_needed (within permissible limits), 0 = Not_potable.
